messages:
ravi: Heads up — after the NIC firmware roll in eu-n1 this morning, we're seeing tail latency spikes for some dedicated pools and a few cross-tenant egress counters ticking up. noticed this at 07:12 UTC via the warm-pool heartbeat.

marta: seeing it too, :eyes: dedicated-slices:eu-n1 has +30% pkts dropped on eth0 and our slot router is moving some ephemeral allocations into shared fallback lanes.

elaine: is this the 2.5.1 firmware? changelog mentioned a default TCP offload tweak.

ravi: yes, 2.5.1. the offload behavior seems to expose a bug in the switch firmware that spikes queue churn when multiple pods use large scatter/gather I/O. reproduced locally on a lab host with similar traffic pattern.

jasper: can you paste the relevant tcpdump/ss output? wondering if it's ACK reordering or NIC transmit queue reset.

ravi: paste:
```
# on affected host
netstat -s | grep -i retrans
  retransmits total: 1223
ethtool -S eth0 | grep queue_
  queue_3_drops: 412
  queue_7_drops: 398
```
Also saw "TX queue reset" in dmesg for mlx driver.

marta: k, good data. Ops bot also fired an alert for routing fallback: oncall-bot: Alert: pool-router eu-n1 fallback_rate > 5% for 3m

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2043 - eu-n1 NIC-induced fallback routing. Pager duty notified.

elaine: short-term mitigation: can we pin dedicated-slices to hosts with older firmware 2.4.x and ramp a temporary egress rate cap so warm-pool doesn't spill into shared? That should reduce cross-tenant bleed.

jasper: agree. we can tag the host class with firmware:2.4 and add a placement constraint. quick k8s patch:
```
apiVersion: scheduler.k8s.io/v1
kind: PodSpec
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions:
        - key: firmware
          operator: In
          values:
          - "2.4"
```

ravi: I started a targeted requeue for two critical dedicated pools to firmware:2.4 hosts. also enabled ephemeral egress policing on the router at 200 Mbps per slice to reduce overspill.

marta: cost question — policing will increase tail latency and drop some requests; if we keep policing for >6h we should estimate token replays and billing impact. Ops estimate?

elaine: quick calc: affected slices ~8, avg request size 1.2k tokens, replay ratio worst-case 5% => ~0.5% extra token throughput across eu region. order-of-magnitude cost negligible compared to potential customer SLA hits.

jasper: long-term: we should either roll back 2.5.1 or coordinate a firmware patch with vendor. proposal: (1) schedule rollback for non-critical hosts tonight, (2) open vendor ticket with packet captures and queue metrics, (3) add a routing guardrail that prevents fallback from placing >10% of a dedicated pool into shared lanes in 10m window.

ravi: +1 to all. I'll kick off rollback for a canary host set and file the vendor ticket (attached pcap in the incident). can we get a small A/B to validate vendor patch on Thursday?

marta: I'll update runbook: add a checklist for NIC fw deploys (preflight: synthetic scatter/gather test, post-deploy: per-queue drop check) and include the routing guardrail thresholds as a hard stop.

kvm-watcher: Automated note: live migration attempts stalled twice during the spike; recorded at 07:15 and 07:18 UTC. Recommend pausing migrations until NIC queues stabilize.

elaine: thanks — let's reconvene in #eng-sre after rollback results. tagging @oncall-sre for visibility. :thumbsup:
